title: S2G-RAG: Structured Sufficiency and Gap Judging for Iterative Retrieval-Augmented QA

visual_explainer.question: How does S2G-RAG turn sufficiency and missing-information gaps into the next retrieval action?
visual_explainer.takeaway: The controller explicitly separates 'is current evidence sufficient?' from 'what is missing?', then maps structured gap items into the next retrieval query while keeping a compact evidence memory.
visual_explainer.compared_with: Iterative RAG that conditions the next search on raw reasoning/provisional answers without an explicit structured gap state.

analysis.tldr: S2G-RAG makes retrieval progress explicit: a lightweight judge predicts whether accumulated evidence is sufficient and, when it is not, emits structured missing-information items that deterministically become the next retrieval query.
analysis.problem: Multi-turn RAG can answer from incomplete evidence or keep retrieving redundant text because the controller lacks a clean representation of what has been established and what remains missing.
analysis.core_idea: Maintain a sentence-level Evidence Context and use S2G-Judge to output either sufficient or structured gap items; gap items drive the next query, separating evidence-state representation from the answer reasoner.
analysis.agent_loop: Accumulate compact evidence → judge sufficiency → if insufficient predict gap items → construct next query → retrieve/extract → update evidence → repeat or answer
analysis.retrieval_design: The judge is a LoRA-tuned Llama-3.2-3B controller distilled from GPT-4o-mini traces; retrieval uses matched BM25 or E5 settings, with at most four turns and fixed per-turn top-k in the main experiments.
analysis.evidence: Under matched BM25 with the same Llama-3-8B answer reasoner, S2G-RAG reaches 43.3/56.5 EM/F1 on HotpotQA versus 32.7/43.3 for SIM-RAG, and 41.7/48.6 on 2Wiki versus 34.1/40.2. Removing S2G-Judge drops HotpotQA by 15.8 EM and 19.0 F1 while keeping retriever, maximum turns, per-turn top-k, and answer reasoner fixed. The sentence-level extractor also reduces reported per-sample latency by 17.7% versus appending full retrieved text while improving EM/F1.
analysis.why_it_matters: This is a cleaner predecessor for explicit evidence/missing-state control than August-only narratives suggest. It strengthens the claim that state representation is becoming a first-class control object, while separating that idea from document-structure navigation such as DocNavRAG.
limitations: The main setting is benchmark QA with capped retrieval turns and fixed per-turn top-k, so the state controller is not yet a general resource-allocation policy.
Teacher-distilled supervision and a separate evidence extractor add components beyond the sufficiency/gap interface itself.
The strongest evidence is on multi-hop QA; transfer to web, SQL, code, or multimodal retrieval remains open.
